gitCommit.subject: Timer ring + touch-set dial: quiet conic ring, live length dial, gold completion moment (#352)
gitCommit.body:
Timer ring + touch-set dial: quiet conic ring, live length dial, gold completion moment (#352)

* Timer ring + touch-set dial: design spec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Timer spec rev 2: fold adversarial spec review

Blockers fixed: ring token pair must clear 3:1 both ramps (new ring-sweep/
ring-track tokens + CI contrast pairs); expiry semantics corrected (ends the
round, not pause) with dialog-gated commit-on-Done; no-timer state keeps the
adjust affordance; RoundLengthChooser/StartSessionForm blast radius
enumerated; one responsive dialog instead of popover+sheet (also fixes the
phone-e2e-never-runs-in-CI hole); legacy map completes '20'; dial geometry,
handle, focus contract, and keyboard-driven e2e specified.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Timer ring + dial: implementation plan

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): ring sweep/track tokens, AA-gated in both themes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): RoundBoxSeconds model, legacy parsing, feel names, single boxToMs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(timer): own-property legacy lookup, seconds-model header, catch-path tests

- Fix prototype-chain bug: Object.hasOwn(LEGACY_MINUTES, raw) instead of `in`
- Rewrite module comment to describe RoundBoxSeconds model (30s steps, 30–300s)
- Add throwing-storage tests exercising catch fallbacks
- Add constructor edge-case test to verify prototype-key exclusion

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(timer): consumers on RoundBoxSeconds, single converter

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): TimerRing shared conic-gradient ring

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): RoundTimer renders the quiet ring, digits sr-only, no-timer keeps the affordance

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): touch-set dial + Done-gated mid-round dialog; chooser retired

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(timer): dialog focus return, pointercancel, persist pin

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): start form sets length on the dial

Replace the Select component for round length with TimerDial, changing state
from string to RoundBoxSeconds type and persisting immediately in onChange.
Port tests to use keyboard-driven dial interaction with localStorage assertions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(timer): gold ring completion moment in the recap

Add a quiet gold ring badge to the "what moved" recap when the round had a timer,
positioned above the heading as an aria-hidden marker of completion. The badge uses
TimerRing with expired state (gold band + checkmark). Meaning stays with the recap's
existing live-region text. TDD: failing tests first, then implementation wired to all
three hosts (TriageRound, UsageRound, RoundSurface).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(timer): round end closes the length dialog (badge race)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(timer): drop dead TIMEBOX_OPTIONS mirror from form test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(timer): pin dialog-close-on-round-end in triage and usage hosts

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(timer): e2e ring journey, wired into CI's sort area

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(timer): e2e asserts the recap badge, honest sr-only check, CI timing headroom

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(timer): final-review fixes — beat holds under dialog, badge-disc contrast pin, expiry gold assertion, test hygiene

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* sync-docs: DESIGN.md documents the timer ring token pair

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
